chapter: Eddie Heywood, the organ and later work
title: Basin Street East house pianist; subbing for Duke
summary: He played intermission piano and for acts at Basin Street East, and once filled in with Duke Ellington's band during Mel Torme's engagement.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Then I went back on piano at the Basin Street East. I stayed there for, oh, quite a few years.
Well, at Basin Street East what did you do? Accompany singers who came in and...?

No, I just played intermission piano. I played for some acts. A comedian I played for, Rich Little; I played for Bobby Vernon or... You know, when they didn't have music or anything, I would play for them. And it became a sort of a dependable engagement.
I remember once you were accompanying some singer
there, and you took Duke's place in his band, didn't you. Do you remember that?

Oh yeah. Well, Duke had to go to... That was on the Mel Torme thing. Mel Torme wanted first preference on the marquee or something, so Duke Ellington promptly just recorded with the... I think it was the Dallas Symphony Orchestra. He took off! So there was nobody to play. I was handy, and I played, you know...
But I remember another time there was a girl singer, and you accompanied her with the band. He was there then.
Not famous, but... Hinton or something like that.
Funny, when I went to Paris, Jimmy Davis... She met Jimmy Davis, and he (?) also; he helped her a lot in Paris. She must have made some money.
This same girl. What was her name...?
I think it was a name like Hinton or something like that.
I can get it from Jimmy.
Well, she wasn't really big-time, was she.
She wasn't bad. Sy Oliver remembers her. She had some recordings here.
